item.title: 50 Cent Targets Tia Kemp’s Backup Accounts As Their Internet War Continues
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 50 Cent claimed Tia Kemp's backup page was down and named TikTok and Twitter as his next targets after her livestream rant.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent kept pushing to get Tia Kemp off social media, claiming her backup page was down and telling her TikTok and Twitter were next after she accused him of getting her main accounts restricted.

The latest round moved beyond Kemp’s earlier complaint that she could no longer use Instagram Live.

In one Instagram post, 50 shared a screenshot of a small backup account bearing her name and a bio claiming her previous page had been deleted at 800,000 followers.

“Back up down, Tik Tok and Twitter next,” he wrote.

He also posted what appeared to be a message confirming that a Facebook account had been reviewed and removed for violating Meta’s Community Standards.

The screenshot did not identify the account or establish who sent the message. He paired that post with *NSYNC’s “Bye Bye Bye.”

“Bye Bye, this my sh!t right here *NSYNC this joint knock,” 50 wrote.

The posts followed Kemp’s TikTok Live attack on the Queens rapper.

Rick Ross’ former girlfriend blamed 50 and his followers for reporting her pages and cutting off her access to audiences on Instagram and TikTok.

“You ugly. You done reported my IG. I can’t go live, you loving Diddy,” she said.

Kemp aimed another stretch of the rant at his supporters, accusing them of joining the reporting effort.

“All you 15 Cent fans done reported my pages, Crab in a bucket. Oh, you wipe your mouth. Get off your knees. He hate black people. He white. You can’t take a African-American black woman like me. I’mma lose my voice cussing you out for a million days and nights.”

50’s posts made clear he wanted more of her accounts gone.

Their fight intensified after 50 mocked an alleged October 11 assault on William Roberts III, Kemp’s adult son with Ross.

William told police a man threatened him with a gun and struck him in Daytona Beach. 50 offered help to the accused attacker, drawing Kemp into the dispute.

Kemp then targeted 50’s teenage son, Sire Jackson, and his mother, Daphne Joy. On October 26, 50 filed a separate federal lawsuit in Los Angeles seeking at least $6 million on Sire’s behalf.

His lawyers accused Kemp of fabricating a diagnosis for the boy and making sexually degrading claims about Joy.

Kemp had already mocked the damages demand with a fake fundraiser. During the latest live stream, she again dismissed the prospect of paying him.

“We rich over here forever. I wouldn’t let him spend two pennies if we was settled for that. You won’t get one cent out of two cent if the judge said I owed you,” she said.

There was also a Florida protective-order case involving Sire.

A temporary injunction required Kemp to stay 500 feet away and barred direct or indirect contact.

The November 3 hearing on longer restrictions was delayed because she had not been served, with the next hearing set for December 7.

Kemp still promised her audience that the suspensions would not end her online presence.

“I will be back after my suspension of Tik Tok and IG,” she declared.

item.title: Charlamagne Tha God Praises Democrats For Putting Economic Concerns First
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Charlamagne Tha God praised Democratic candidates for focusing on household costs as he discussed the midterm election results.
item.content:encoded:
Charlamagne Tha God found a reason for hope in the Democrats who ran in the midterms: their attention to the bills people had to pay.

On “The Breakfast Club” on November 4, he praised the party’s candidates as the crew discussed the election results with Black Information Network journalist Mimi Brown.

“The quality of candidates on the Democratic side, I have never been more optimistic about in my life,” Charlamagne said.

He credited their focus on household finances over culture wars. His praise centered on what candidates offered voters and the issues they chose to address.

The conversation followed “The People’s Election Night,” which brought “The Breakfast Club” and “Native Land Pod” together for the November 3 vote.

The special’s episode description placed the four-hour live show at New York City’s Manhattan Center. Angela Rye, Bakari Sellers and Andrew Gillum joined the radio team for coverage billed as including reports from the rural South.

The program’s stated concerns included access to health care, the cost of housing, schools and paths to a better income. Those were also the kinds of day-to-day pressures Charlamagne pointed to when he explained his optimism the next morning.

His praise came days after he questioned Nicki Minaj’s political reasoning on the same show. During the October 29 broadcast, he challenged her description of New York Governor Kathy Hochul as evil, even though she supported Donald Trump and Hochul’s Republican opponent, Bruce Blakeman.

Charlamagne said Minaj had the right to choose whom she backed. He objected to the different moral standards he believed she applied to the politicians.

“That’s selective outrage, if you ask me,” he said.

The Associated Press called for Democrats to take control of both chambers of Congress. AP’s voter polling found anger over high prices, inflation, the Iran war and corruption. The gains included districts Trump carried in 2024, even as the Democratic Party itself remained unpopular with many voters.

Democrats also faced pressure to turn their gains into a check on Trump, even with voters still skeptical of the party.

The new majorities would give Democrats the votes to resist Trump’s legislative agenda and nominations, as well as the power to investigate his administration.

item.title: Terrell Owens Calls Jay-Z Super Bowl Pick A Conflict Of Interest
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Terrell Owens questioned Jay-Z's dual Super Bowl role and argued that Lil Wayne deserved a shot at the halftime spotlight.
item.content:encoded:
Terrell Owens thinks Jay-Z’s place on the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage raises a basic fairness question.

The Pro Football Hall of Famer challenged the decision during his Get TO The Point podcast after the NFL named Jay-Z as the February 14, 2027 headliner at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

“I think it’s a conflict of interest,” Owens said.

His argument centers on Roc Nation’s role with the league. Jay-Z’s company has worked as the NFL’s strategic entertainment adviser and has helped shape the halftime show since 2019. Roc Nation will also executive produce the upcoming performance.

Owens questioned why someone involved in the process would end up with the slot himself. He said other performers had earned a chance and singled out Lil Wayne.

“I think Lil Wayne deserves an opportunity,” Owens said, pointing to the New Orleans rapper’s worldwide audience.

The criticism lands differently once the NFL’s version of the decision is added. Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had asked Jay-Z to perform from the beginning of the Roc Nation partnership.

Goodell said his one request was “that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him.”

That official account suggests the league had been pushing the idea for years, rather than Jay-Z simply putting his own name at the top of the list.

The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Jay-Z’s set on October 26. It will be the first Super Bowl halftime performance led by the Brooklyn rapper, whose company has helped produce shows featuring Shakira and Jennifer Lopez, The Weeknd, Rihanna, Usher, Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny.

Owens did leave room to be won over. He said the show could change his view if Jay-Z used the moment to bring out artists who had been passed over, including Lil Wayne. He argued that a guest appearance by one of those performers would show the headliner had listened to years of criticism about the selection process.

That makes Owens’ complaint more than a simple attack on Jay-Z. He is asking who gets access to the biggest stage in music and whether the person helping to open that door should also walk through it.

For now, the NFL is standing behind its choice, and Jay-Z has described the booking as the next step in a 30-year journey from Reasonable Doubt to the Super Bowl. Owens will be watching to see who else gets invited along.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Lil Durk Faces Contraband Investigation As Feds Fight His Release
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Durk faced a federal contraband investigation as prosecutors used alleged jail violations to oppose his latest bail request.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Durk is under federal investigation over allegations he helped bring contraband into the Los Angeles jail where he remained locked up after beating his murder-for-hire case.

Prosecutors disclosed the investigation in a November 4 filing opposing his latest request for bail. They accused the rapper of using unauthorized devices to make hundreds of calls and argued his conduct behind bars showed he could not be trusted on release.

“The government is also investigating additional, potential criminal violations related to [Lil Durk] facilitating the introduction of contraband at the MDC,” prosecutors wrote.

That disclosure appeared in a footnote in the government’s response to Lil Durk’s bond application before Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald. The filing described an ongoing investigation, without announcing a new contraband indictment.

The government tied that inquiry to broader complaints about his access to phones inside the Metropolitan Detention Center.

“Among other violations, [Lil Durk] has repeatedly attempted to conceal his communications by using other inmates’ phone access, engaging in impermissible three-way calls, and smuggling in and using contraband communications devices to make hundreds of phone calls,” prosecutors alleged.

Prosecutors also said Lil Durk had been disciplined for possessing a contraband cellphone and attempting to destroy it. They accused him of refusing another cell search the previous week, after asking the court to let him await trial outside jail.

“Just last week, [Lil Durk] refused to comply with instructions from BOP staff attempting to search [Lil Durk]’s prison cell for yet more contraband,” the government wrote.

The bail fight grew out of the prosecution that began with Lil Durk’s October 2024 arrest. Authorities accused him of financing an August 2022 attack targeting Quando Rondo in Los Angeles as revenge for King Von’s killing. Quando Rondo survived, but his cousin Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson was killed.

Jurors acquitted Lil Durk of all five charges on September 11, 2026. He remained detained because murder-in-aid-of-racketeering and firearm charges had been separated for another trial.

Those remaining allegations included the January 2022 killing of Stephon Mack outside a Chicago community center.

Prosecutors alleged Lil Durk used Only The Family’s money and influence to reward violence against rivals. Lil Durk pleaded not guilty.

The government expanded the case in June 2026. Anthony Montgomery-Wilson and Preston Powell, accused of carrying out Mack’s killing, had pleaded guilty that spring. Their pleas admitted to a paid killing, but neither man named Lil Durk while entering his plea.

Lil Durk’s attorneys disputed a direct connection between him and Mack’s death. The judge separated the new counts, allowing the original murder-for-hire trial to proceed first.

In the new bail opposition, prosecutors insisted the acquittal did not resolve the remaining allegations.

“He still faces the more serious and expansive criminal allegations that he chose not to go to trial on,” they wrote.

Lil Durk’s latest release proposal offered future music and branding income as security, alongside property and support from friends. Sony backed a guarantee capped at $1 million.

Jay-Z also submitted a letter urging the judge to weigh the acquittal and allow Lil Durk home under court-imposed restrictions.

Prosecutors rejected the celebrity support as a reason for release and questioned whether a private security company paid by Lil Durk could adequately supervise him.

“His actions in an already-restrictive condition of confinement show he cannot and will not abide by bond conditions on his own accord, outside the purview of the USMS and BOP,” they argued.

The remaining trial was moved to August 30, 2027. Prosecutors said the delay largely reflected defense lawyers’ scheduling conflicts and offered to proceed sooner.

“The government remains prepared to proceed to trial on a more expedited schedule,” the filing stated.

item.title: Talib Kweli’s Daughter Revives Nkiru Bookstore With Brooklyn Celebration
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Talib Kweli's daughter Diani Eshe Greene led a Brooklyn celebration for Nkiru Bookstore's revival, carrying on a family legacy.
item.content:encoded:
Talib Kweli‘s daughter, Diani Eshe Greene, led Nkiru Bookstore’s online revival, hosting a Brooklyn celebration that put books and Hip-Hop on the same bill.

The gathering in Bed-Stuy featured Kweli behind the DJ decks while Diani hosted and performed, BKReader reported.

Diani, 27, described herself as an artist who was taking event curation more seriously.

“I feel extremely fulfilled to be able to put this together and continue the legacy of my dad, my grandmother and Leothy Miller,” she said.

Nkiru began in 1976 under founder Leothy Miller Owens. Kweli and Mos Def bought it in 1998. Its physical shop closed in 2002.

The store previously operated as the Nkiru Center for Education and Culture, a nonprofit centered on literacy and multicultural awareness.

Jessica Care Moore, Rasheed Chappell and Punchline were among the speakers. Wiki, HRLUM and David Jame$ also performed.

Books by Alice Walker and Mikki Kendall were also on display.

That link between rap and reading has long been part of Kweli’s life. In a July 2007 AllHipHop interview, he spoke about the strain of keeping a bookstore running as his music career grew.

“Maintaining a book store is hard enough, but doing it amidst a burgeoning rap career was harder,” Kweli said then.

His reading habits reached far beyond other rappers’ work. Kweli named Miles Davis’ autobiography as his favorite and pointed to David Ritz’s Marvin Gaye biography, “Divided Soul,” as another book he loved.

He also recalled studying history and religion during his bookstore years, while reading books by rappers including Ice-T, LL Cool J and Snoop Dogg.

By the time of that interview, he was building a home library. Kweli said he had spent about $700 at Borders, buying some titles he had already read because he wanted them on his own shelves.

The online book section at KweliClub now lists Kweli’s own “Vibrate Higher: A Rap Story” alongside RZA’s “Tao of Wu” and M.K. Asante’s “Buck: A Memoir.”

Poetry and fiction also have a place: the catalog includes Jessica Care Moore’s “We Want Our Bodies Back” and Jacqueline Woodson’s “Another Brooklyn.”

item.title: Run-DMC Joins Aerosmith Two Days After DMC’s Freeway Crash
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Run-DMC joined Aerosmith for "Walk This Way" at the Hollywood Bowl just two days after DMC was involved in a freeway crash.
item.content:encoded:
Run-DMC joined Aerosmith for “Walk This Way” at the Hollywood Bowl on November 1, two days after DMC was involved in a Los Angeles freeway crash.

The appearance followed a collision on October 30 that prompted his management to update AllHipHop on the rapper and the other people involved.

“Yes he’s okay, they got into a accident on the freeway but everyone is okay,” a representative told AllHipHop.

The collision involved a garbage truck. Video obtained by AllHipHop showed DMC standing and talking with fire department personnel.

NBC Los Angeles reported that DMC complained of minor pain. The California Highway Patrol received the collision call at 11:43 A.M. that Friday on the eastbound 105 Freeway near the 110 Freeway.

By Sunday night, he and Rev Run were part of Aerosmith’s closing set in Los Angeles. The band played seven songs to finish the second of its two “California, Dream On: Aerosmith & Friends” shows.

Aerosmith began “Walk This Way” before stopping to bring out the rap duo.

“This song ain’t the song without some people,” Steven Tyler told the crowd from the stage.

Rev Run and DMC entered from opposite sides of the stage. Aerosmith drummers Joey Kramer and John Douglas both played on the song as the groups performed together.

Tyler also pointed to the history they shared: “We broke through the wall together and showed the world what they was missing.”

The performance carried a reminder of their 1986 collaboration, too. Joe Perry used the same Guild X-100 Bladerunner guitar he played in the original “Walk This Way” video.

Run-DMC had been announced for the Hollywood Bowl shows on October 7, weeks before the crash. The official bill covered the October 29 and November 1 concerts and said the guest lineup would vary by night.

Guns N’ Roses, the Black Crowes and Heart performed songs from Aerosmith’s catalog before the band took over for its own set.

Despite host Bill Burr describing the concerts as Aerosmith’s last shows, Tyler rejected that idea on November 1. The Hollywood Bowl appearance ended the two-show run without settling the band’s future.

item.title: 1 Rapper That Should Have Blown Up by Now
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Indianapolis rapper Vette Rey refuses to stay in one lane. With a 33-track album, performances alongside hip-hop legends, and a genre-bending sound, is she one of rap’s most overlooked talents?
item.content:encoded:
Indianapolis artist Vette Rey has the catalog, stage experience, and fearless approach to music that make you wonder why her name isn’t in more conversations.

Some rappers spend their entire careers trying to find their lane. Vette Rey apparently missed the memo about having to stay in one.

The Indianapolis native is a rapper, singer, songwriter, actress, and performer who moves between hip-hop, R&B, and rock without worrying too much about where one genre ends and another begins.

She calls herself the “Queen of Versatility,” and while plenty of artists love giving themselves impressive titles, Vette Rey has made a point of building a catalog that backs up her artistic ambitions.

But here’s the interesting part. She’s not exactly new to this. She’s been recording, performing, developing her brand, and putting in the kind of work that usually comes before a major breakthrough.

So why isn’t Vette Rey a bigger name?

33 Songs. Three Chapters. Zero Interest in Playing It Safe.

In an era when artists are encouraged to release short projects, chase viral moments, and keep feeding the algorithm, Vette Rey took a different approach.

She released Vette Views, a sprawling 33-track album divided into three musical chapters.

Thirty-three songs.

That’s not an EP designed to test the waters. That’s an artist opening the doors to her entire creative world and inviting listeners to explore.

The project moves through themes of love, ambition, relationships, personal growth, and confidence. Songs including “12,” “Overtime,” “BX3,” “Lie to Me,” and “Shooting Star” help introduce the different sides of her musical identity.

The approach is ambitious, especially for an independent artist competing for attention in an industry where a song sometimes gets only a few seconds to make its impression.

But Vette Rey doesn’t seem particularly interested in making herself easier to categorize.

And that might be one of her greatest strengths.

She’s Shared Stages With Legends. Now It’s About Building Her Own.

Vette Rey has already experienced something many aspiring rappers dream about: opening for established hip-hop artists.

Her performance history includes appearances supporting Project Pat and Lil Flip, two names with their own places in Southern hip-hop history.

Those opportunities matter. Performing in front of audiences who didn’t necessarily come to see you requires confidence, preparation, and the ability to make an impression.

But opening for recognizable artists is only one chapter of the story.

The bigger challenge is turning those opportunities into an audience that shows up specifically for you.

That’s the next level Vette Rey is working toward.

The Industry Loves Versatility. Until It Has to Market It.

Here’s something worth considering.

The music business constantly celebrates artists who break boundaries. Yet much of the machinery built to promote them still depends on categories.

Are you a rapper? An R&B singer? A rock-influenced performer? What playlist do you belong on? Which audience is supposed to discover you first?

For an artist like Vette Rey, those questions aren’t necessarily simple.

Her musical identity includes all three genres, and she has built her independent career around the freedom to explore them.

That creates an interesting opportunity, but also a challenge. Versatility can introduce an artist to several audiences, yet it takes strong songs, consistent visibility, and a recognizable identity to bring those audiences together.

Vette Rey is betting that her personality and creative range can become the connection.

Outside of music, she’s also developing her presence through live performances, visuals, merchandise, and entertainment ventures.

She’s not simply trying to release another record. She’s trying to build something people recognize.

Maybe You’ve Been Sleeping on Vette Rey

Nobody can guarantee which artist will have the next breakout moment. Talent alone doesn’t guarantee success, and an extensive catalog doesn’t automatically translate into mainstream recognition.

But the interesting artists aren’t always the ones dominating your timeline.

Sometimes they’re the ones building in plain sight.

Vette Rey has a 33-song project, experience on stages alongside recognizable hip-hop names, and an artistic identity that refuses to be squeezed into one category.

She’s already done a lot of the groundwork. Now she needs more ears on the music.

And if the “Queen of Versatility” gets the attention she’s working toward, don’t expect her to suddenly start following the rules.

Vette Rey isn’t waiting for somebody to give her a lane. She’s busy creating her own.

Listen:

Follow Vette Rey on Instagram, and discover more at VetteRey.com.

item.title: Justin Timberlake’s Reported “Tell-All” Revisits Janet Jackson Fallout & Britney Spears
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Justin Timberlake's reported Apple doc will revisit Janet Jackson's Super Bowl fallout and address Britney Spears' comments.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Timberlake is reportedly bringing his history with Janet Jackson and Britney Spears to Apple TV in a four-part documentary series set for December.

Variety reported that three sources confirmed the project, which Fisher Stevens is directing. The series was described as a “tell-all,” with Jackson’s 2004 Super Bowl appearance and Spears’ recent comments among the expected topics.

One source said Jackson would discuss the halftime-show incident. Another said Timberlake would address some of Spears’ recent comments, although the report did not identify which remarks. It also did not establish whether Jackson’s contribution would be a new interview or archival material.

Apple and representatives for Timberlake and Jackson declined to comment or did not respond. The project has not been officially announced.

Jackson addressed the Super Bowl fallout herself in her four-hour 2022 documentary, which aired on A&E and Lifetime. During the 2004 performance, Timberlake pulled away part of her costume and exposed her breast. Jackson took a disproportionate share of the backlash.

In that documentary, Jackson described the incident as an accident and said she wanted the public to move forward. She also explained that Timberlake offered to speak out afterward. Jackson said she told him not to because she did not want the controversy directed at him.

Jackson also said she and Timberlake were still very good friends.

“He and I have moved on, and it’s time for everyone else to do the same,” Jackson said.

Their Super Bowl history resurfaced when Timberlake invited her to join his 2018 halftime performance. Jackson declined because she did not want to relive the ordeal.

The renewed attention also follows Timberlake’s 2021 public apology.

AllHipHop previously covered that apology while reporting on a separate documentary about Jackson’s Super Bowl fallout being developed by the filmmakers behind “Framing Britney Spears”.

“I am deeply sorry for the times in my life where my actions contributed to the problem,” Timberlake wrote in his social media apology.

That earlier Jackson project and the reported Apple series are separate productions.

Timberlake previously worked with Apple on the 2021 film “Palmer”. Last month, he also joined Jay-Z onstage in Paris, a rare appearance after his tour ended in July 2025.

item.title: Cardi B Reveals Son Grey On His First Birthday
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cardi B revealed her son Grey's name and face on his first birthday, sharing a message about the strength he gave her.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B finally put a name and face to the youngest member of her family as she celebrated his first birthday.

The Bronx rapper revealed Wednesday (November 4) that the son she shares with NFL receiver Stefon Diggs is named Grey.

The Instagram birthday post also included the first clear photos of the toddler’s face, one year after Cardi kept his name out of public view.

“Happy 1st birthday to Grey M.D!!” she wrote. Cardi said carrying him through an uncertain and high-pressure period gave her extra strength. She added, “I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life!”

The photos show Grey sitting on a bed in a baseball cap and dressed in a doctor’s costume for Halloween. Cardi also told him he had changed what a “Grey day” meant to her because his smile, laugh and spirit light up her life.

Grey was born on November 4, 2025. Cardi announced the birth nine days later and shared hospital photos that showed her with Diggs and their newborn, but she did not reveal his name or show his face. She preserved his umbilical cord as gold jewelry, another personal keepsake from the pregnancy.

The pregnancy unfolded during a demanding stretch. Cardi publicly confirmed it in September 2025 while promoting Am I the Drama? and preparing for a tour.

She described herself then as happy, strong and powerful even while balancing work with pregnancy. When Grey arrived, she framed the birth as another reason to become the best version of herself for her children.

Grey is Cardi’s fourth child and her first with Diggs. She shares Kulture, Wave and Blossom with estranged husband Offset. Diggs is also a father to daughters Nova and Charliee from previous relationships.

Cardi used “Baby Brim” and other nicknames while keeping Grey’s identity private. Even her initial hospital carousel concealed his face.

That makes Wednesday’s post more than another birthday gallery: it is the first time she has publicly connected the name, face and birthday in one place.

The birthday reveal lands differently from the usual celebrity baby-name rollout. Cardi framed Grey’s arrival as part of a difficult chapter, then centered the post on the emotional lift he gave her.

After a year of nicknames and carefully cropped images, she used his birthday to introduce him on her own terms.

item.title: Jamie Foxx Welcomes Third Child, First With Alyce Huckstepp
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jamie Foxx and Alyce Huckstepp have welcomed their first child together, making the actor and musician a father of three.
item.content:encoded:
Jamie Foxx is a father of three after welcoming his first child with girlfriend Alyce Huckstepp.

PEOPLE confirmed the birth Wednesday (November 4) through sources close to the couple. Foxx’s representatives had not responded to the publication when its report went live, and the baby’s name, sex and exact birth date were not disclosed.

The new arrival is Huckstepp’s first child and Foxx’s third. The actor and musician is already a dad to Corinne Foxx, 32, and Anelise Bishop, 18, from previous relationships. He shares Corinne with Connie Kline and Anelise with Kristin Grannis.

The pregnancy was first reported in May. TMZ reported at the time that Huckstepp was several months along, although the couple kept the due date and sex private. AllHipHop also covered the pregnancy announcement when it surfaced.

Foxx joked about becoming a new father at 58 during an August interview. He said the idea felt less intimidating after talking with Al Pacino, who welcomed a child in his 80s.

The comparison brought some perspective, but Foxx still stopped short of turning the pregnancy into a running public update. He and Huckstepp let the months pass without disclosing a name, due date or gender.

Foxx, 58, and Huckstepp, 31, were first linked publicly in 2023. Reports of a split followed in January 2025, but the pair were photographed together again that spring and later in Miami. Their relationship returned to the spotlight this week when Foxx discussed plans to surprise Huckstepp with a home in Australia.

Foxx has long kept parts of his family life private while speaking openly about fatherhood. In a previous PEOPLE interview, he said one of the best parts is watching his daughters “light up when you come into a room.”

He also described helping them solve problems he had already faced himself.

That balance remains intact. The family shared enough to confirm the birth, but not enough to fill in the personal details.

The restraint matters because several reports have treated those missing details as invitations to speculate. None of the reviewed sources established them.

The family update closes the loop on the pregnancy news without adding details the couple has chosen not to share. For now, the confirmed development is simple: Foxx and Huckstepp have welcomed their first baby together.
